learned_operations: Split a new English-language NDA into exact runtime substrings and use those substrings as evidence rather than storing training-document quotations.

Recognize affirmative disclosure permissions, access restrictions that imply limited permission, and exceptions to nondisclosure clauses; resolve linked recipient definitions such as Representatives or Affiliates.
Bind employee and third-party permissions only to actual authorized receiver groups, including need-to-know, purpose, confidentiality, responsibility, and written-authorization qualifications.
Exclude mentions of a disclosing party's employees or practice staff from Receiving Party employee scopes.
Extract return-or-destroy obligations together with their actual termination, request, or other trigger instead of treating survival language as a termination trigger.

Create post-return retention permissions only when retention is explicitly coupled to return or destruction through an exception, temporal phrase, archival/backup qualification, or adjacent return clause.

Mark a public query unresolved when an authorization uses an unresolvable recipient label or a retention clause refers to an unavailable antecedent; otherwise mark the supported query families complete so absence can yield NotMentioned.
limitations: The procedure is lexical and targets conventional English NDA drafting; unusually fragmented clauses, tables, OCR corruption, or distant cross-references may remain unresolved.
It does not infer that directors, officers, staff, or generic Representatives are employees unless employee/personnel wording or a linked definition supports that scope.
It does not convert a generic prior-written-consent exception, a bare right to retain information, or survival of confidentiality duties into permission to retain after return or destruction.
Legal conclusions requiring unstated agency relationships, corporate-control facts, or interpretation beyond the document's express receiver groups are intentionally left unsupported.
